newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip, eye U.S. economic indicators.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip, eye U.S. economic indicators.

text.p: Argentine bonds slipped Monday in thin activity after strong U.S. economic indicators.

Traders said the market was marked lower because of a strong U.S. August new home sales report, but activity was hampered. "Not a lot happened today, many investors have closed their books for the month and the quarter," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.10 to 118.10, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 83-3/4.
Market players said this week's performance was likely to be determined by U.S. economic indicators with the key September jobless report due on Friday.
On Tuesday, the National Association of Purchasing Manager's (NAPM) index and auto sales for September will be released.

Otherwise, traders in London said Argentina's $750 million 10-year global bond is likely to be launched on Tuesday. It is expected to be priced 435-450 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note.

The bond pricing, coming just after Senate passed into law the government's tax hiking package last week, is expected to give an indication of how easy it will be for Argentina to raise funds next year, when some $11 billion needs to be raised, and through the remainder of this year.
According to statements by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez in New York over the weekend, some $1.8 billion and 1.5 billion pesos remains to be issued this year.
"We expect financing to be readily available in 1997," said financial consultants I.D.E.A. in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.98 percent from 5.88 percent.
